findings.title: Shard path now interpolates the same queries repeatedly (once up front, again per sub-request)
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls applyTemplateVariables on every target. Each shard-group sub-request is then passed to runSplitQuery, which this PR also changed to call applyTemplateVariables on every target. DataSourceWithBackend.query() interpolates once more when runQuery executes. So each query is interpolated 1 + N + N times, where N is the number of shard groups and time chunks. Each pass re-runs addAdHocFilters, which does a Loki AST parse and rewrite. Ad-hoc filters are re-applied to already-filtered expressions, and text that is already interpolated is run through the template engine again. The result is wasted CPU on every sub-request, plus a risk of re-substituting `$…` text that was produced by a first-pass variable value. Interpolate once at the top-level entry point, or have the shard path tell runSplitQuery to skip re-interpolation.

findings.title: Test hard-codes the redundant interpolation count (5 calls)
findings.body: The assertion changed from `interpolateVariablesInQueries` being called once to `applyTemplateVariables` being called 5 times. That is 1 call from runShardSplitQuery plus 4 from runSplitQuery, one per sub-request. The test pins the double interpolation as expected behaviour. It will break whenever the number of shards or groups changes, and it will fail if the redundancy is later fixed. It should assert that interpolation happened and that the final queries are correct, not the exact call count.

findings.title: Empty-expression filter runs before interpolation
findings.body: Targets are filtered with `.filter((query) => query.expr)` before `applyTemplateVariables`. A query whose expression is only a variable that resolves to an empty string, such as `$myQuery`, therefore survives as an empty expr after interpolation. It then flows into `isLogsQuery`, `querySupportsSplitting`, `calculateStep` and the request, instead of being dropped as an empty query. The same ordering is used in shardQuerySplitting.ts (hide and expr filters before the map). The old shard code filtered after interpolation, so this is a behaviour change there. Run the empty-expression filter after the interpolation map.

findings.title: New interpolation tests do not cover scopedVars or ad-hoc filter forwarding
findings.body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' tests only exercise the mocked `replace` on `$__auto` and `$step`. Nothing verifies that `request.scopedVars` and `request.filters` are forwarded to `applyTemplateVariables`, which is the new contract in both runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery. Nothing verifies that ad-hoc filters end up in the executed sub-queries. There is also no test that the interpolated step is what feeds `calculateStep` for grouping, which is the point of the fix. A regression that drops the filters argument would pass these tests.
